metaDescription: Six electric kettles that are easy to lift, from a 0.6 L mini to a 1.8 L glass model, compared on capacity, wattage, cordless base and boil-dry safety.
introParagraphs: A lightweight kettle is mostly a question of how much water you carry. Water weighs about one kilogram per liter, so a 1.7 L kettle adds roughly 1.7 kg to whatever the empty body weighs, while a 0.6 L kettle adds a fraction of that. Few listings state an empty weight, which means capacity is the most reliable guide to how heavy a kettle feels when you lift it to pour.

This guide covers six electric kettles that make sense for a lighter lift, from a 0.6 L stainless mini that states its weight to a 1.8 L glass kettle that boils fast but holds a lot of water. We evaluated each one based on product specs and buyer feedback patterns, looking at capacity, wattage, cordless base, auto shutoff and boil-dry protection, and how easy the lid and spout are to use. We left out stovetop kettles and duplicate color listings.

No kettle here is the lightest on every measure. The small ones are easy to lift but need refilling for a group, and the large ones reward you with more hot water per boil but are heavier to pour when full. The comparison below shows how to pick the trade that suits your kitchen and your hands.

products.name: Hamilton Beach 1 Liter Electric Tea Kettle
products.description:
The Hamilton Beach is a 1 liter electric kettle rated at 1500 watts, built with a rapid-boil system that the maker says is faster than a microwave. It lifts cord-free off its base for serving, and it has automatic shutoff with boil-dry protection. The listing calls the plastic BPA free and targets college dorms and small kitchens.

At 1 liter it holds about four mugs, which is plenty for one or two people and far less to lift than a 1.7 L kettle. A full kettle carries about one kilogram of water, so it stays manageable when you pour with one hand. The tradeoff is capacity: a group or a big pot of tea needs a second boil, and the listing does not state an empty weight.

Compared with the 0.6 L WTJMOV, the Hamilton Beach holds more and boils with much more power, but it is not as compact. Against the 1.8 L Chefman, it is the easier lift and takes less counter space. It is the balanced choice if you want a small body that is not tiny.
products.bestFor: One or two people who want an easy lift with room for four mugs.

products.name: WTJMOV 0.6L Small Electric Tea Kettle
products.description:
WTJMOV states a weight of 1.34 pounds for this 0.6 liter electric kettle, the only pick in this guide with an empty weight in the listing. It is a double wall stainless steel kettle with a separate lid, auto shutoff and a 600 watt element. The maker says it boils 0.6 liters in about five minutes.

The stated weight and small capacity make it the easiest kettle here to lift and pour, and a full kettle adds only about 0.6 kilograms of water. A separate lid is easy to fill and clean. The tradeoffs are speed and size: 600 watts is slow compared with 1500 watt kettles, and 0.6 liters fills only two or three cups, so it suits one person.

Compared with the Hamilton Beach at 1 liter and 1500 watts, the WTJMOV is lighter and more compact but much slower and smaller. Against the Chefman 0.8 L gooseneck at 1000 watts, it offers less speed and no pour-over spout, but it has a double wall body and a weight you can check. Choose it for desk, bedside or travel.
products.bestFor: Solo users who want the lowest lifting load and a stated weight.
pros: States a 1.34 lb weight, rare in this category
0.6 liter fill adds little water weight

Separate lid fills and cleans easily
cons: 600 watts takes about five minutes to boil

products.name: Chefman Gooseneck Electric Kettle 0.8L
products.description:
The Chefman gooseneck is a 0.8 liter kettle with a 1000 watt element, a gooseneck spout for controlled pouring and one-touch operation. The maker says it boils in as little as three minutes, the body lifts off the base for cordless pouring, and blue LED lights show when it is heating. The listing also states boil-dry protection.

The 0.8 liter size keeps the full load near 0.8 kilograms of water, so it is gentle on the wrist, and the gooseneck lets you pour slowly with little tilting force. The narrow neck is harder to clean and fill than a wide-mouth kettle, which is the main tradeoff. It holds less than the Hamilton Beach at 1 liter, so a second boil is common.

Compared with the WTJMOV at 600 watts, the Chefman is quicker and gives better pouring control, but it has no stated weight and a single-wall look. Against the 1.8 L Chefman, it is far lighter to lift but holds less than half the water. It is the pick when controlled pouring matters more than volume.
products.bestFor: Pour-over coffee and tea drinkers who want slow, precise pouring.

products.name: OVENTE 1.7L Electric Tea Kettle KP72W
products.description:
The OVENTE KP72W is a 1.7 liter kettle with a 1100 watt element, a concealed stainless steel heating plate and BPA-free construction. The listing says it has auto shutoff and boil-dry protection and a removable spout filter, and it comes in white or black finishes. The maker says it is more energy efficient than higher wattage models.

The benefit is capacity: 1.7 liters covers several cups per boil, which reduces trips. The cost is lifting load, because a full kettle adds about 1.7 kilograms of water, so fill only what you need when lightness matters. At 1100 watts it boils a bit slower than the 1500 watt models, and the listing gives no removable lid or empty weight.

Compared with the Chefman 1.8 L at 1500 watts, the OVENTE draws less power and fills slightly less, but it is plastic rather than glass. Against the Hamilton Beach at 1 liter, it holds 70 percent more water and weighs more when full. It suits a household that wants volume with a plastic body.
products.bestFor: Households that boil for several cups and fill partially for lighter lifting.

products.name: Chefman Electric Kettle 1.8L 1500W Glass
products.description:
The Chefman 1.8 liter kettle pairs a 1500 watt element with a glass body, a removable lid for cleaning, auto shutoff and boil-dry protection. The maker says it boils water in about three minutes and lifts off its base for cordless serving. Glass lets you see the water level and any scale on the walls.

It is the largest kettle here, so a full fill adds about 1.8 kilograms of water on top of the glass body. That is a real lift for tired wrists, and the sensible habit is to fill it to what you need. The advantage is speed and volume: 1500 watts boils more water faster than the 1100 watt OVENTE, and the removable lid makes cleaning simple.

Compared with the WTJMOV at 0.6 liters, it holds three times the water but is far harder to lift when full. Against the Cosori at 1.7 liters, it is bigger and quicker but has a glass body rather than a no-plastic-contact design. Pick it if volume and speed matter more than a light pour.
products.bestFor: Families that boil a lot of water and will fill it only as needed.
pros: 1500 watts boils in about three minutes
Glass body shows water level and scale
Removable lid for easy cleaning
Auto shutoff and boil-dry protection
cons: 1.8 liter fill is heavy when full
Glass is more fragile than steel or plastic

products.name: Cosori Electric Kettle 1.7L No Plastic Contact
products.description:
The Cosori 1.7 liter kettle is designed so water never touches plastic, according to the maker. It has a wide mouth and a large-angle lid that make filling and cleaning easy, and the maker says it heats 0.5 liters in under three minutes. Auto shutoff is listed on the product page.

The wide opening is the practical benefit, since you can reach in with a hand to scrub scale and fill from a tap without aiming. The tradeoff is size: 1.7 liters of water weighs about 1.7 kilograms, so the full kettle is a similar lift to the OVENTE. The listing gives no empty weight or wattage, so judge heaviness by capacity.

Compared with the Chefman 1.8 L glass kettle, the Cosori is slightly smaller and aimed at water purity and easy cleaning rather than speed. Against the 1 liter Hamilton Beach, it holds more but is heavier to pour when full. Choose it if wide-mouth cleaning and a plastic-free water path outweigh lightness.
products.bestFor: People who want an easy-to-clean wide mouth and no plastic touching water.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Water weighs about one kilogram per liter, so capacity changes how heavy a kettle feels more than body material does. The WTJMOV at 0.6 liters adds about 0.6 kg when full, while the Chefman 1.8 L adds about 1.8 kg. For one or two people, 0.6 to 1 liter is enough. If you buy a larger kettle, fill it only to what you need.

Most listings do not give an empty weight, so you cannot rank kettles by body mass alone. The WTJMOV is the one pick here that states 1.34 lb. If lightness is your priority, look for a stated number rather than the word lightweight. When no number is given, use capacity as your guide.

Higher wattage boils faster, which also means less time holding a full kettle. The Hamilton Beach and Chefman 1.8 L are 1500 watts, the OVENTE is 1100 watts and the WTJMOV is 600 watts at about five minutes. A slow kettle is fine on a desk but frustrating at breakfast. For daily use, 1000 watts or more is a sensible floor.

A cordless kettle lifts off a 360 degree swivel base so you carry no cord to the table. The Hamilton Beach and Chefman picks both lift off their bases for serving. A gooseneck spout like the Chefman 0.8 L gives slow, precise pouring with less tilt. Check that the handle fits your whole hand.

Auto shutoff and boil-dry protection are separate features, and a listing should state both. The Hamilton Beach, OVENTE, Chefman 1.8 L and WTJMOV all list auto shutoff, and several name boil-dry protection. Most kettles in this class use a steam sensor, so the water must reach a full boil before power cuts. Do not buy a kettle that states neither.

Scale builds on the element over time and lengthens boil times, so you want to see and reach it. The Cosori has a wide mouth and large-angle lid, and the Chefman 1.8 L has a removable lid. Gooseneck spouts like the Chefman 0.8 L are harder to clean. Descale on a regular schedule, whichever kettle you choose.

howWeEvaluated.title: Lifting load
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared capacity and any stated weight to estimate how heavy each kettle feels when full. The WTJMOV at 0.6 liters and 1.34 lb leads, and the Chefman 1.8 L at 1.8 liters is the heaviest to lift. Kettles that give no weight were scored by capacity.

howWeEvaluated.title: Boil speed
howWeEvaluated.description: We read wattage and boil claims from each listing. The Hamilton Beach and Chefman 1.8 L at 1500 watts lead, the OVENTE at 1100 watts follows, and the WTJMOV at 600 watts is slowest at about five minutes.

howWeEvaluated.title: Pouring and handling
howWeEvaluated.description: Spout design, cordless base and lid access were assessed based on product specs. The Chefman 0.8 L gooseneck leads for controlled pours, and the Cosori wide mouth leads for filling. Kettles with fixed cords lost points.

howWeEvaluated.title: Safety features
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked that each listing states auto shutoff and boil-dry protection. The Hamilton Beach, OVENTE and Chefman picks all name boil-dry protection. Listings that left out either feature scored lower.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cleaning and upkeep
howWeEvaluated.description: Opening size, removable lids and material were compared. The Cosori leads with a wide mouth, and the Chefman 1.8 L has a removable lid and visible glass. Narrow necks and hidden scale lowered the score.

faq.q: Which of these kettles is the lightest?
faq.a: The WTJMOV is the only pick that states an empty weight, at 1.34 lb, and it holds just 0.6 liters. For the rest, capacity is the best guide. The Chefman 0.8 L and Hamilton Beach 1 L are the next easiest to lift when full.

faq.q: How much does water add to the weight?
faq.a: Water weighs about one kilogram per liter. A full 1.7 or 1.8 liter kettle adds about 1.7 to 1.8 kilograms on top of the body. Filling only to what you need cuts the lift.
Yes, it stops the element from scorching if the kettle runs out of water. Auto shutoff is a separate feature that stops heating at the boil. Check that a listing states both.

faq.q: Is a 600 watt kettle too slow?
faq.a: The WTJMOV at 600 watts boils 0.6 liters in about five minutes per the maker. That is fine for a desk or travel but slow for daily family use. A 1000 to 1500 watt kettle like the Chefman 0.8 L or Hamilton Beach boils much faster.

faq.q: Are gooseneck kettles harder to use?
faq.a: They pour slowly and precisely, which suits pour-over coffee and lowers the tilt needed. The narrow neck is harder to clean and fill than a wide-mouth kettle like the Cosori. Choose one if control matters more than convenience.

faq.q: How often should I descale a kettle?
faq.a: Descale when you see white buildup or notice slower boils. Glass kettles like the Chefman 1.8 L show scale easily, and wide mouths like the Cosori make scrubbing easier. In hard water areas, plan on every few weeks.

faq.q: Does glass make a kettle heavier?
faq.a: Glass can add body weight compared with thin plastic, though listings rarely give figures. Capacity matters more, since a full 1.8 liter glass kettle carries 1.8 kilograms of water. Glass also shows the water level, which is helpful for filling just enough.
